units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Wrings his hand.
Yours is a rare nature. Well, you shall be helped with your Sailors' Home. That you may rely upon.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: ENGSTRAND tries to thank him, but cannot for emotion.
Hangs his travelling-bag over his shoulder.
And now let us set out. We two will go together.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: At the dining-room door, softly to REGINA.
You come along too, my lass. You shall live as snug as the yolk in an egg.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Tosses her head.
Merci !
units.name: REGINA

units.text: She goes out into the hall and fetches MANDERS' overcoat.
Good-bye, Mrs. Alving! and may the spirit of Law and Order descend upon this house, and that quickly.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Good-bye, Pastor Manders.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She goes up towards the conservatory, as she sees OSWALD coming in through the garden door.
While he and REGINA help MANDERS to get his coat on.
Good-bye, my child. And if any trouble should come to you, you know where Jacob Engstrand is to be found.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: Softly.
Little Harbour Street, h'm--!
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: To MRS. ALVING and OSWALD.

And the refuge for wandering mariners shall be called "Chamberlain Alving's Home," that it shall! And if so be as I'm spared to carry on that house in my own way, I make so bold as to promise that it shall be worthy of the Chamberlain's memory.
units.name: ENGSTRAND

units.text: In the doorway.
H'm--h'm!--Come along, my dear Engstrand. Good-bye! Good-bye!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: He and ENGSTRAND go out through the hall.
Goes towards the table.
What house was he talking about?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oh, a kind of Home that he and Pastor Manders want to set up.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: It will burn down like the other.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: What makes you think so?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Everything will burn. All that recalls father's memory is doomed. Here am I, too, burning down.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: REGINA starts and looks at him.
Oswald! You oughtn't to have remained so long down there, my poor boy.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Sits down by the table.
I almost think you are right.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Let me dry your face, Oswald; you are quite wet.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: She dries his face with her pocket-handkerchief.
Stares indifferently in front of him.
Thanks, mother.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Are you not tired, Oswald? Should you like to sleep?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Nervously.
No, no--not to sleep! I never sleep. I only pretend to.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Sadly.
That will come soon enough.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Looking sorrowfully at him.
Yes, you really are ill, my blessed boy.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Eagerly.
Is Mr. Alving ill?
units.name: REGINA
